The wedding reception was not a formal, stiff affair held under glittering chandeliers in a rented ballroom; it was an intimate, joyful celebration that spilled out from the drawing room into the grand library. Music played softly in the background—a rich blend of classical piano and acoustic jazz—while guests laughed, shared stories, and toasted the newlyweds with vintage champagne.

Julian stood by the tall arched windows of the library, holding a crystal flute of champagne in one hand while his other arm remained securely wrapped around Clara’s waist as she rested her head against his shoulder.

"You know," Clara murmured softly, watching Marcus and her father debate the finer points of algorithmic logistics near the hearth, "if someone had told me three years ago, when I was working sixty-hour weeks trying to keep my head above water, that I’d end up marrying the most powerful man in New York inside a historic snow-covered fortress, I would have told them they were completely insane."

Julian smiled, pressing a gentle kiss to the top of her head. "And if someone had told me when I was sitting in that wheelchair, surrounded by sharks who wanted to strip my company down to the bone, that my entire life would be saved by a quiet, brilliant woman with a clipboard and a kind heart, I would have said the same thing."

He turned her slightly so he could look down into her eyes, his expression turning serious and intensely tender. "You didn't just save my company, Clara. You saved my soul. You reminded me that power without empathy is just a gilded cage, and that the only wealth worth having is the kind you share with someone who loves you for who you are, not what you own."

Clara smiled, her eyes shining with unshed tears of pure happiness. She reached up, her fingers tracing the sharp line of his jaw. "We're a team, Julian. Equal partners. Through the boardroom battles, the courtroom fights, and every quiet morning yet to come."

"Always," Julian answered, leaning down to capture her lips in a sweet, lingering kiss.

Across the room, the fire crackled warmly against the winter night, casting a golden glow over the books, the laughter, and the unbreakable foundation they had built together.
